23:2. **Network:** the ESP32 and laptop share a phone hotspot (2.4 GHz). Set `LAPTOP_IP` in `config.h` to the laptop's address on the hotspot, and allow Python through the Windows firewall.
62:| The glove sends to one laptop's address, not broadcast (2026-11-07) | Broadcast over the phone hotspot lost about a third of the samples, in gaps of up to about 350 ms, enough to swallow a whole punch. Sending to one address gets WiFi's automatic re-sends. To use another computer, flash its address |
66:| A phone can be the right arm's sensor instead of a glove (2026-11-07) | The phyphox app serves the phone's accelerometer and gyroscope and the laptop polls it (`phyphox_imu.py`). It is chosen with `--phone ADDRESS` together with `--arm right` in `punch_capture.py`, `punch_tune.py` and `punch_live.py`, or `--right-phone` in `punch_live_both.py`, and is refused for the left arm so the left glove's recordings and model can't be mixed with it. Polling means nothing has to connect into the laptop: in testing, a phone's connection into the laptop never arrived (from a teammate's hotspot or an iPhone's own), while the laptop reaching the phone worked. The right arm's recordings, model and punches stay as for the right glove. A phone has no magnetometer and reports about 80 to 100 Hz against a glove's 500 Hz. Capture's "enough data" check used to assume 500 Hz and rejected every phone recording as dropped packets (shown as MISSED); it now scales with the sensor's measured rate (`LiveSensors.sample_rate_hz`). A browser-page alternative (`phone_imu.py`) is kept but did not work in that test |
90:**Right arm from a phone:** `phyphox_imu.py` polls the phyphox app and plugs into `LiveSensors` through `--phone` (with `--arm right`). The receiver has run on a real phone (about 80 to 100 Hz). 60 right-arm punches (20 each of CROSS, HOOK and UPPERCUT) were recorded with it, and `models/punch_rf_right.joblib` was trained on them: 98% cross-validated, but from one session, so optimistic. It has no NONE (not a punch) examples yet and has not been tried live. `phone_imu.py` with `phone/index.html` is a browser-page alternative that did not work (see the decision above).
